_general_note: Per the state eligibility memo: 'Any World Language Level III-VI (including AP World Languages)' satisfies the ss.world_perspectives diploma requirement. Levels I-II do not. Also relevant: Enrollment Honors Seal requires at least 4 World Language credits.

courses.title: French I

prerequisites.note: Recommended C or better in English

courses.description: Most instruction is in the target language. Encourages interpersonal communication through speaking and writing, providing opportunities to exchange information on familiar topics, understand/use appropriate greetings, and write short passages with guidance. Emphasizes reading and listening comprehension, examining the practices, products, and perspectives of the target culture. Oral participation is required, including pronunciation drills and presentations.

courses.title: French II
courses.description: Requires a sound understanding of vocabulary and grammatical structures from the first year. Encourages interpersonal communication through speaking and writing, making/responding to requests in familiar situations, and writing with greater independence. Emphasizes reading/listening comprehension using contextual clues. Students describe the practices, products, and perspectives of the target culture and make connections across content areas.

courses.title: Spanish III
special_notes: Slower pace than Spanish III Honors; recommended for students not planning Spanish IV Honors or collegiate study
courses.description: Recommended for students who don't plan to take Spanish IV Honors or study Spanish at the collegiate level. Covers the basic material of Spanish III Honors at a slower pace, with more opportunities to practice and strengthen language skills. Requires a sound understanding of first-year vocabulary/grammar, encouraging interpersonal communication, reading/listening comprehension, and connections across content areas including art, music, history, literature, and government.

courses.title: French III Honors
special_notes: Teacher recommendation; B or higher in prior level recommended
courses.description: A challenging continuation of coursework at a faster pace, taught entirely in the target language. Requires a sound understanding of vocabulary and grammar from the first two levels, encouraging interpersonal communication through initiating/sustaining/closing conversations and exchanging detailed information. Emphasizes continued development of reading/listening comprehension and connections to art, music, history, literature, and government.

courses.description: Provides context for continued development of language skills and cultural understanding beyond the classroom, with more opportunities to exchange written/oral information and an emphasis on speaking practice and listening strategies. Includes critical analysis of literary, musical, and artistic genres through authentic materials like short stories, poetry, and novels, with well-organized compositions in the target language.

courses.title: American Sign Language I
special_notes: CONFIRMED by owner: no prerequisite for Year 1 (2156). Earlier apparent contradiction in source doc resolved.
courses.description: Gives students a peek into Deaf culture while building critical vocabulary skills necessary to communicate with other ASL users. For students fascinated by watching two people communicate with their hands, who want to learn a unique language not offered at many Indiana high schools.

courses.title: American Sign Language II
special_notes: CONFIRMED by owner: requires having earned credit for the previous year's course (2156).
courses.description: Continues the focus on frequently used signs through a functional-notional approach and discussion of the deaf community's cultural features, with emphasis on further developing receptive and expressive communication skills. Students watch and understand short stories, dialogues, and poetry in ASL, develop visual discrimination skills, understand various ASL dialects, begin using classifiers, and continue mastering the GLOSSING writing system.

courses.title: American Sign Language III
special_notes: CONFIRMED by owner: requires having earned credit for the previous year's course (2158).
courses.description: Continues focus on students' non-verbal communication skills at advanced competency levels, using ASL exclusively as students communicate using more complex structures moving from concrete to abstract concepts. Provides opportunities to express oneself in advanced situations using sophisticated vocabulary, apply advanced grammatical features, and discuss topics related to historical and contemporary events within the deaf community.
